title: Wall Street is 'tiring of the Bank of Nvidia, the Bank of AMD and the Bank of Broadcom': Baird's Mortonson
key_facts: Baird tech strategist Ted Mortonson told Yahoo Finance the AI sell-off is increasingly about who needs financing and what it costs.
He said the street is 'tiring of the Bank of Nvidia, the Bank of AMD and the Bank of Broadcom'.
He pointed to a higher cost of capital and scrutiny of 'circular finance' coming out of the Anthropic research meeting.
Anthropic reportedly told investors at a closed meeting that third-quarter revenue rose to $16.8 billion.
CoreWeave fell more than 15% on Wednesday and again in pre-market trading on Thursday; Mortonson named CoreWeave, Nebius and Oracle as near the bottom of tech on free cash flow.
A new Gartner forecast says most neocloud providers will 'cease independent operations' by 2030.
The PHLX Semiconductor Index was up about 87% for the year on 6 Oct and 65% at Wednesday's close; Mortonson calls the pullback 'healthy' and thinks money is moving to software.
quote_evidence: I think the street is tiring of the Bank of Nvidia, the Bank of AMD and the Bank of Broadcom
Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) reportedly told investors at a closed meeting that its third-quarter revenue climbed to $16.8 billion.
why_it_matters_hint: One strategist's view that financing cost, not just AI demand, is now driving AI share prices.
notes: Yahoo Finance's own interview with Ted Mortonson (Senior Reporter Brooke DiPalma); it is the original. The meaning of 'circular finance' is the usual market usage, not defined in the article.
